issue_title: [feature] wire ChannelRegistry into main.rs and surface active channels in runtime introspection
issue_body:
### What problem does this solve?

`ChannelRegistry` (`crates/genie-core/src/channel/mod.rs`) is the data structure #564's own foundational commit built specifically to close the M2 "channel and session adapters" epic's loop.
Its own doc comment states its purpose plainly:

> Tracks the channels active in a process so responses can be routed back to the transport they came from.

Verified directly: `ChannelRegistry::new()`/`::default()` is never called anywhere outside `channel/mod.rs`'s own unit tests.
A repo-wide grep for `ChannelRegistry` outside that one file returns nothing.
`register()`, `len()`, `by_kind()`, `kinds()` — every method on the type — is exercised only by its own test module, never by the running daemon.

This gap is becoming more visible, not less, as the epic completes: voice is now ported onto `Channel` (#700, merged), Telegram is being ported next (#701, open; #783 just landed its reference adapter).
Once all three transports genuinely implement `Channel`, there will be three fully-conformant `Channel` values running in `main.rs` — and still no single place that tracks any of them.
The abstraction #564 built to answer "which channels are active in this process" exists, compiles, and is tested in isolation, but is completely disconnected from the real running system.

I also traced `main.rs`'s actual startup shape while investigating this, since the module doc comment ("Runs two interfaces concurrently: HTTP chat API... Stdin text mode... In production, a third interface is added: Voice pipeline") doesn't match the code: voice mode and HTTP(+Telegram) mode are mutually exclusive (`if voice_mode { ... } else if interactive { repl } else { chat_server + optional telegram via tokio::try_join! }`), not three concurrent interfaces.
That makes "which channel(s) is this instance actually running" a real, non-obvious operational question with no current answer beyond reading logs — exactly the gap `ChannelRegistry` was built to close.

This is not a duplicate of #564 (tracks porting the three transports onto the `Channel` trait itself, not wiring the registry that already exists), #700/#701/#783 (the individual transport ports), or #565/#702/#774 (session continuity, a different concern from channel-instance tracking). None of those issues mention `ChannelRegistry` or propose instantiating it. Confirmed via search: zero open or closed issues reference `ChannelRegistry`.

### Proposed feature

- `main.rs`: construct one `ChannelRegistry` at startup and `register()` whichever channel(s) this process actually runs (the voice channel in voice mode; the HTTP channel and, when enabled, the Telegram channel in daemon mode).
- Expose what's registered through existing runtime introspection rather than inventing a new surface: extend `RuntimeContract`/`build_runtime_contract_snapshot` (`crates/genie-core/src/runtime_contract.rs`, `server.rs:1970`) with an `active_channels: Vec<String>` field (sourced from `ChannelRegistry::kinds()`), so `/api/runtime/contract` reports it alongside the existing prompt/tool/policy hashes.
- Design question to resolve: should `active_channels` be folded into the *hashed* part of the contract (`contract_hash` would then change if the channel mix changes across a restart — arguably correct, since that's exactly the kind of deployment drift `RuntimeContract`'s own doc comment says it exists to catch), or kept as an unhashed, informational sibling field? Worth deciding explicitly rather than guessing.
- `crates/genie-api/src/routes.rs`: proxy the enriched contract the same way `get_runtime_contract` already proxies `/api/runtime/contract` today — no new endpoint needed if the field rides along on the existing one.
- Dashboard (`crates/genie-core/dashboard/index.html` / `dashboard.js`): surface `active_channels` wherever the dashboard already renders the runtime contract, so an operator can see at a glance whether this instance is running as a voice appliance or a chat/Telegram daemon.
- Tests: a `channel::tests` case asserting `ChannelRegistry` reflects what `main.rs` actually registers (via a thin integration seam, not a full daemon boot), plus a `runtime_contract` test asserting `active_channels` matches the registered kinds.

### Alternatives considered

- **Leave `ChannelRegistry` as an internal, untested-in-production convenience type and don't wire it up** — cheapest, but leaves dead code sitting in the middle of the M2 channel-boundary epic's own core abstraction, which reads as unfinished work once #701/#783 land and all three transports are "ported" without ever being tracked anywhere.
- **Fold `active_channels` into the runtime contract** (recommended above) — reuses an existing, already-hashed, already-dashboarded introspection surface instead of adding a new endpoint.
- **New dedicated `/api/channels` endpoint instead** — cleaner separation of concerns (channel liveness isn't really a "prompt/tool/policy contract" concept), but adds a new route, a new `genie-api` proxy function, and a new dashboard panel instead of extending something that already exists. Worth the maintainer's call on which fits the introspection surface's intended shape better.

### Which milestone is this aimed at?

M2 — Portable providers and channel boundaries

### Privacy / security considerations

No new data leaves the device — `active_channels` is a small enum-derived string list (`"voice"` / `"http"` / `"telegram"`), already implied by which config flags are set, not new sensitive information. If folded into the runtime contract, it's exposed exactly where prompt/tool/policy hashes already are today (local-only `/api/runtime/contract`, already behind the existing origin/token gate).

### Additional context

- `crates/genie-core/src/channel/mod.rs` (`ChannelRegistry`, `register`, `kinds`, `by_kind`) — the existing, currently-unused type.
- `crates/genie-core/src/main.rs` — confirmed no `ChannelRegistry::new`/`::default` call anywhere; also confirmed the actual voice-vs-daemon mutual-exclusivity shape (lines ~292–464) that motivates surfacing this at runtime rather than only in deploy-time config.
- `crates/genie-core/src/runtime_contract.rs` (`RuntimeContract`, `RuntimeContractSummary`) and `server.rs:1970` (`build_runtime_contract_snapshot`) — the natural extension point.
- `crates/genie-api/src/routes.rs` (`get_runtime_contract`) — already proxies this exact endpoint; would carry the new field with no route changes.
- Related, non-duplicate issues: #564 (parent channel-trait epic), #700 (voice port, merged), #701/#783 (Telegram port, open/landing), #565/#702/#774 (session continuity — a different concern).
